USD.catalyst: The US dollar index holds firm in uptrend territory above its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages as markets digest resilient domestic growth and hawkish Federal Reserve rate prospects driven by recent upside inflation and employment surprises. The greenback continues to draw support from liquid dollar reserve allocations and persistent interest rate differentials, with SOFR at 3.91%. Geopolitical escalation in the Middle East—highlighted by naval mine strikes east of the Strait of Hormuz—further reinforces safe-haven demand. Market focus shifts to upcoming monetary policy guidance, with Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michael Barr scheduled to speak alongside the release of the latest FOMC meeting minutes.

GBP.catalyst: Pound sterling trades near multi-month lows against the dollar at 1.3081, moving below its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages despite stronger-than-expected UK retail sales data showing a 0.7% month-over-month expansion in October. While the Bank of England maintains its official Bank Rate at 3.75% with a persistent tightening bias, sterling gains remain capped by broader US interest rate dynamics. The currency faces headwind pressures as markets weigh the relative pace of central bank policy paths, leaving sterling vulnerable to shifts in global rate expectations. Traders now look ahead to upcoming UK preliminary PMI figures and central bank commentary to gauge policy trajectory into year-end.

EUR.catalyst: The euro remains under pressure near 1.0969 against the dollar, trading entirely below its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages as market participants navigate European Central Bank policy expectations. Leveraged funds hold a substantial net short position of -105,891 contracts, leaving the single currency exposed to a potential short squeeze even as the euro faces a 147-basis-point OIS carry penalty against dollar assets (€STR at 2.44% versus SOFR at 3.91%). Fiscal frictions are also coming to the fore after the French presidency office described the latest EU budget proposal as "very disappointing" and not a foundation for agreement. Market participants are looking to the upcoming preliminary S&P Global Manufacturing and Services PMIs for fresh domestic growth signals.

JPY.catalyst: The Japanese yen has outperformed its G10 peers over the one-week horizon, advancing +1.82% as Middle East supply disruptions and equity liquidations fuel risk-off safe-haven demand. Spot USD/JPY trades near 158.50, capped beneath the key 160 threshold where intervention warnings and market caution intensify. Underlying price pressures remain elevated following Tokyo core-core CPI accelerating to 3.0% year-over-year from 2.0%, with market participants pricing in the possibility of Bank of Japan policy rate increases reaching 2.5% by mid-2027. Investors are monitoring the upcoming national CPI release on November 20 and the next Bank of Japan policy meeting for definitive signals on rate normalization.

AUD.catalyst: The Australian dollar has registered sharp G10 underperformance over the one-week period (-2.33%), falling to 0.6615 and extending a technical breakdown well below its 20-day moving average of 0.6883. Despite the Reserve Bank of Australia lifting its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% on November 3, 2026—its fifth hike of the year—a divided 6-3 vote structure and back-to-back domestic job losses undercut expectations of further tightening. Leveraged funds reduced AUD net long exposure by 15,052 contracts to +26,143, reflecting deteriorating economic sentiment. The immediate outlook hinges on the monthly CPI indicator scheduled for November 25 alongside preliminary S&P Global PMI releases and economic developments in China.

CAD.catalyst: The Canadian dollar demonstrates steady performance across G10 crosses, supported by solid domestic consumption indicators as Canadian retail sales expanded 0.8% in the latest release, with core sales rising 1.0%. Spot USD/CAD trades near 1.4349, positioned above its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages while driven by a 136-basis-point short-term rate differential (SOFR at 3.91% against CORRA at 2.55%). Market positioning remains heavily tilted against the loonie, with leveraged funds holding -75,447 net short contracts despite pricing an 58% probability of a rate hike. Key upcoming catalysts include Canada’s trade negotiations as Ottawa seeks an interim US tariff agreement by year-end, ahead of the Bank of Canada's policy decision on December 9.

NZD.catalyst: The New Zealand dollar trades near multi-year lows at 0.5467 against the US dollar, remaining anchored below its 20-day moving average of 0.5579. Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Anna Breman stated in Dunedin that while persistent oil price gains could push inflation somewhat higher than previously projected, New Zealand's economic recovery remains uneven with businesses struggling to pass along elevated costs. Domestic trade dynamics remain constrained following an October trade deficit of NZ$2.8 billion against a NZ$2.1 billion prior deficit. Markets are looking to upcoming RBNZ policy communications and regional demand trends to assess whether the currency can find a stable floor.

NOK.catalyst: The Norwegian krone shows signs of stabilizing in spot markets, trading near 9.779 against the US dollar above its 20-day moving average of 9.454, though it remains lower over a one-week horizon. Norges Bank recently held its policy rate unchanged while explicitly leaving the door open to future rate increases, citing strong terms of trade and resilient domestic growth. However, upside momentum for the krone faces ongoing headwinds from softening global crude oil prices, which historically weaken Norway’s external balances. Investors are looking to upcoming Norwegian energy sector investment data and Norges Bank policy guidance to gauge whether interest rate differentials can offset commodity-related drag.

SEK.catalyst: The Swedish krona trades under modest pressure, with USD/SEK at 10.236 above its 20-day moving average of 9.950, reflecting a -1.54% decline across G10 crosses over the past week. Domestic fiscal policy has come into focus after the Swedish National Debt Office raised its budget deficit forecasts to 103 billion Swedish crowns for 2025 and 93 billion crowns for 2026. Meanwhile, central bank officials, including Riksbank Deputy Governor Göran Hjelm, emphasized in recent public remarks that monetary policy must remain strictly forward-looking during upcoming Finance Committee hearings. Market participants are looking toward the next Riksbank rate-setting meeting and upcoming domestic inflation prints for clearer directional drivers.
